instructions:
Transpareo holds a workspace's products, components and Digital
Product Passports. Start with me to learn what the credential
allows. For a new product call product_property_types before
create_product. For passports of an existing product call
dpp_requirements, then validate_dpp before create_dpp. A passport
of a batch or an item names its lot in batchIdentifier and the lot
is created with the first passport that names it; there is no
separate lot step. list_lots shows the lots a product already
has. A run of passports goes through bulk_create_dpps with the
lot in shared. publish_dpp
signs the passport and cannot be undone. Recalling a unit is a
status change to suspended through append_dpp_event, not a void;
void_dpp is for a unit that no longer exists. void_dpp and
supersede_dpp need the confirm argument with the stated phrase.
A spreadsheet you have read goes in through import_spreadsheet as
rows keyed by the column headers, never as base64; when it
answers a preview, take the suggestion of every column with a
match, ask the person one short question per column with
matchType none, and call again with the same rows and mappings,
using create_new for columns that should become property types. Set auto where
the mapping is clear: the headings are those of the import
template, or ones you have already seen resolve in this
workspace. While a column has no match, work from the preview.
A run started earlier, or in another session, is found with
list_imports or list_exports and read with wait_for_task on its
statusUrl.
A question about how a person does something in the application
manager is answered from the help articles: search_help for the
topic, then read_help for the article. The API guide describes the
calls a program makes; the help articles describe the screens a
person uses.
Anything without a tool: search_operations, then call_api. Lists
are paged; follow nextPage. Keep every answer short: what was
done, what was found, the one decision that is open.

tools.name: append_dpp_event
tools.title: Append an event to a DPP

event.description: The event to append. `eventType` decides the branch - `status_change` drives a status transition and requires `status`; every other type records a plain event. The versioned types are not accepted here, they ride their own operations.

eventType.description: `status_change` drives the transition and is recorded as an event of type `lifecycle_transition`; every other value is recorded verbatim. `recall` records an authority-only note and moves the passport nowhere - recalling a unit is a `status_change` to `suspended`. A versioned type answers 422 `EVENT_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED` - those ride the void / supersede / reissue / publish operations instead.

status.description: The status to move to. Required on `status_change`, ignored otherwise. `suspended` is the recall and regulatory-hold status: a unit that is still in the field and must stop being used is moved there, and its passport stays readable so whoever scans the code learns of the recall. Voiding is for a unit that no longer exists.

gln.description: GS1 Global Location Number of the place the event happened. Falls back to the calling consumer's GLN, then to the workspace GLN.

publish.description: Seals the event into the Vault (and, for a status change, into a new registered version) instead of leaving it as a pending draft. Honours the publish-debounce window.

data.description: Free-form metadata carried onto the event

eventType.description: Versioned types (`published` ... `corrected`) ride a registered version; local types (`inspection` ... `validation_warning`) do not.

statusFrom.description: The passport status before the transition. Only on `status_change` events.

statusTo.description: The passport status after the transition. Only on `status_change` events.

tools.name: import_spreadsheet
tools.title: Import a spreadsheet
tools.description: Run a spreadsheet import whole: the rows go up, the columns are mapped, the rows are checked and then written. Send the sheet as rows, one object per row keyed by the column headers, which costs the tokens of the sheet itself; data with fileName carries a file as base64 for a format you cannot read, at most 750 KB of bytes. A sheet whose columns are not all resolved comes back with its preview and nothing is written; every column carries a suggestedAction and a matchType, so take the suggestion for attribute, exact and fuzzy matches, ask the person one short question per column with matchType none, and call again with the same rows and mappings, create_new for a column that should become a property type. A sheet with rows the dry run cannot write comes back with those rows and none of it lands. With auto the run needs no preview: the columns are mapped as the mapping form would prefill them and the rows are written in one call. Set it where the mapping is clear, meaning the headings are those of the import template or ones you have already seen resolve in this workspace, and bear in mind that every unmatched column becomes a new property type, which changes the schema of the workspace. While any column is uncertain, leave auto unset and work from the preview. Permission: import_access, and the write permission of the data type to write the rows. Data tier: authorised. Example: import_spreadsheet {"rows": [{"Name": "Aqua", "Origin": "Germany"}]}

rows.description: One object per row, keyed by the column headers; a cell with several values is an array. The cheap way to send a sheet you have read.

data.description: Instead of rows: the file as base64, at most 750 KB of bytes, for a format you cannot read

fileName.description: With data: the name of the file; its extension picks the reader: xlsx, csv, ods or json

valueSeparator.description: What separates several values in one cell

mappings.description: One action per column, the mappings of ImportMappingsInput: map_to_attribute with coreAttribute, use_existing with typeId, create_new with typeName, or skip

options.description: The run options of ImportMappingsInput: backup, published, force, notify

auto.description: Import straight away, for a sheet whose mapping is clear: the headings match the core attributes and the property types the workspace already has, being the headings of the import template or ones you have already seen resolve here. The columns are mapped as the mapping form would prefill them, every column without a matching property type becomes a new property type under its own heading, which changes the schema of the workspace, a clean validation goes on into the import, and what it imports is published unless options.published is false. While a column may have no match, leave this unset, read the preview, take every suggested match, ask the person about the columns with matchType none and call again with mappings.
